items.name: DC cell or battery
items.does: Supplies a steady DC voltage. The longer plate is the positive terminal.
items.use: Torches, vehicles, UPS systems and substation DC supplies for relays and trip coils.
items.tip: Conventional current leaves the + terminal and returns to the − terminal.

items.name: AC source
items.does: A source whose voltage reverses in a sine wave, like the mains supply.
items.tip: A 230 V supply is an RMS value. Its peak is about 325 V.

items.name: Resistor
items.does: Opposes current and turns electrical energy into heat.
items.tip: Ohm's law: I = V / R. Double the voltage and the current doubles.

items.name: Lamp
items.does: Turns electrical energy into light and heat.
items.tip: More current gives a brighter lamp, up to its rating.

items.name: Capacitor
items.does: Stores energy in an electric field. It charges and discharges gradually.
items.tip: After about 5 time constants (5 × RC) it is almost fully charged.

items.name: Inductor
items.does: Stores energy in a magnetic field and resists sudden changes in current.
items.tip: Current rises gradually with time constant τ = L / R.

items.name: Switch
items.does: Opens or closes a circuit by hand.
items.tip: Current flows only when the switch is closed.

items.name: Fuse
items.does: A deliberate weak link that melts when the current is too high for too long.
items.tip: A higher current melts it faster. The heating depends on I² × time.

items.name: Circuit breaker (single-line)
items.does: Opens automatically on overload or short circuit and can be reset.
items.tip: It can also be used as a switch to make and break load current.

items.name: Isolator (single-line)
items.does: Provides an isolating gap, normally operated off load.
items.tip: Open the breaker first, then the isolator.

items.name: Normally open (NO) contact
items.does: Open at rest; it closes when operated.
items.use: Start buttons, relay and contactor auxiliary contacts.
items.tip: NO means no current flows at rest.

items.name: Normally closed (NC) contact
items.does: Closed at rest; it opens when operated.
items.tip: A stop button is wired NC, so a broken wire also stops the circuit.

items.name: Relay or contactor coil
items.does: An electromagnet: when energised it operates its contacts.
items.tip: A small coil current controls a much larger contact circuit.

items.name: Diode
items.does: Lets current flow in one direction only.
items.unit: Rated forward current (A) and reverse voltage (V)
items.tip: A silicon diode drops about 0.7 V when it conducts.

items.name: LED
items.does: A diode that gives light when current flows in the forward direction.
items.tip: Always use a series resistor to limit the current.

items.name: NPN transistor
items.does: A small base current controls a much larger collector current.
items.tip: Ic = β × Ib in the active region, until the transistor saturates.

items.name: Motor
items.body: <line class="ln" x1="0" y1="0" x2="12" y2="0"/><circle class="ln" cx="30" cy="0" r="18"/><text x="30" y="5" text-anchor="middle">M</text><line class="ln" x1="48" y1="0" x2="60" y2="0"/>
items.does: Turns electrical energy into rotation.
items.tip: The shaft speed rises as the supply rises (in this simple model).

items.name: Generator
items.body: <line class="ln" x1="0" y1="0" x2="12" y2="0"/><circle class="ln" cx="30" cy="0" r="18"/><text x="30" y="5" text-anchor="middle">G</text><line class="ln" x1="48" y1="0" x2="60" y2="0"/>
items.does: Turns rotation into electrical energy.
items.tip: Faster rotation gives a higher frequency and a higher voltage (in this simple model).

items.name: Transformer
items.does: Changes an AC voltage using two coils on a common core.
items.tip: V1 / V2 = N1 / N2 for an ideal transformer.

items.name: Current transformer (CT)
items.body: <line class="ln" x1="0" y1="0" x2="60" y2="0"/><circle class="ln" cx="30" cy="0" r="11"/>
items.does: Gives a small, proportional copy of the line current for meters and relays.
items.tip: Never open the secondary of an energised CT.

items.name: Voltage transformer (VT)
items.body: <line class="ln" x1="0" y1="0" x2="14" y2="0"/><circle class="ln" cx="26" cy="0" r="12"/><circle class="ln" cx="40" cy="0" r="12"/><line class="ln" x1="52" y1="0" x2="60" y2="0"/>
items.does: Gives a small, proportional copy of the line voltage for meters and relays.
items.tip: Never short-circuit the secondary of a VT.

items.name: Ammeter
items.body: <line class="ln" x1="0" y1="0" x2="16" y2="0"/><circle class="ln" cx="30" cy="0" r="14"/><text x="30" y="5" text-anchor="middle">A</text><line class="ln" x1="44" y1="0" x2="60" y2="0"/>
items.does: Measures current. It is connected in series.
items.tip: It has very low resistance, so never connect it across a supply.

items.name: Voltmeter
items.body: <line class="ln" x1="0" y1="0" x2="16" y2="0"/><circle class="ln" cx="30" cy="0" r="14"/><text x="30" y="5" text-anchor="middle">V</text><line class="ln" x1="44" y1="0" x2="60" y2="0"/>
items.does: Measures voltage. It is connected in parallel (across the component).
items.tip: It has very high resistance, so it draws almost no current.

items.name: Earth (ground)
items.does: A connection to earth that gives fault current a safe path.
items.tip: Good earthing lets protective devices detect and clear faults quickly.
